candidate.title: hyRAD
candidate.scope: The middle row labelled hyRAD / Hybridization RAD (hyRAD) for degraded DNA in the supplied Illumina poster crop, interpreted as the original Suchan et al. hyRAD architecture using RAD-derived probes to capture a target shotgun library. The left Genome icon with a yellow highlighted segment is genomic context, not a connected material-transfer step. The high-quality-DNA probe branch and the DNA-to-be-captured shotgun-library branch are separate inputs that meet at hybridization. The visible SLAF-seq and Rapture rows, the partial 2b-RAD row, and the unrelated right margin are outside the assigned hyRAD target. ddRAD is an embedded probe-generation component, not an alternative target workflow. Catalogue mentions of other capturable library types and paper-only experimental branches do not add targets or operations. The graph ends at recovered DNA, with readout meaning described at that boundary.

operations.label: Prepare RAD-seq library and size select
operations.description: Convert high-quality genomic DNA into an adapter-bearing, size-selected RAD library used as probe precursors. This is a broad library-preparation block; the primary implementation identifies its reduced-representation component as ddRAD.
operations.mechanism: Restriction-derived library construction and size selection, kept at the combined level shown.
operations.information_effect: Defines the restriction-derived, size-selected genomic subset used for probe production.

operations.label: Adaptor removal and labeling
operations.description: Remove the probe-precursor library adapters and add biotin labels to the RAD-derived DNA fragments, producing capture probes.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper specifies enzymatic restriction to remove adapter sequences, followed by biotin nick labelling. The diagram combines these into one operation.
operations.information_effect: Retains the genomic sequences that determine capture specificity while replacing the adapter-bearing precursor state with a biotinylated affinity reagent. Biotin enables subsequent streptavidin retention.

operations.label: Hybridize to probes
operations.description: Bring the target shotgun library together with the previously produced biotinylated RAD probes; complementary genomic sequences form probe–library hybrids.
operations.mechanism: Sequence-homology-dependent hybridization; the paper explicitly supplies the probe-to-capture route that has no continuous connecting arrow in this compressed drawing.
operations.information_effect: Associates target-library fragments with the affinity-labelled probes by genomic homology. Probe-source restriction sites define probe generation but are not required to remain present in captured target-library DNA.

operations.label: Streptavidin pull down
operations.description: Retain biotinylated probes and their hybridized target-library fragments on streptavidin beads, separating an enriched bound fraction.
operations.mechanism: Biotin–streptavidin affinity connects probes to beads; associated target DNA is retained through probe–target hybridization. The bead is the affinity support, not a second genomic input.
operations.information_effect: Enriches target-library DNA related to the probe subset, with possible background carryover. Bead retention is not proof of perfect specificity.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title, row heading, and verified matching collection-page heading identify hyRAD alone. The primary paper explicitly describes generation of ddRAD-based probes, independent shotgun-library construction, hybridization capture, and sequencing of the enriched target library. All graph operations apply to this depicted hyRAD implementation; the RAD preparation block is its probe-source component. The final release boundary is visible as bead-to-DNA flow and is interpreted using the primary text. This is not a claim that all later hyRAD adaptations have identical preparation.
